solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Island boy taking female group around festival (6)

indicatorNotes.taking: the boy takes the group in, holding it inside
indicatorNotes.around: the whole assembly is turned around, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: I = island, as on maps
a lad is a boy
the WI, the Women's Institute, a British women's organisation

annotation.surface: A lad from an island is escorted round a festival by a party of women.
annotation.walkthrough: I plus LA(WI)D makes ILAWID, which read the other way is the answer. 'Around' looks like it wraps something; here it turns the lot back to front.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the Hindu festival of lights, held each autumn, is one festival among many.

entries.clue: I’ve a pointer for sculpting bust (11)

indicatorNotes.for sculpting: sculpting reshapes material, so the letters are reshaped

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters

annotation.surface: A sculptor explains that a pointing tool is needed to carve a bust.
annotation.walkthrough: In the surface 'bust' is a sculpted head and shoulders; as the definition it means broken. A pointer really is a sculptor's tool, which keeps the picture tight.
annotation.definitionFit: Something bust is broken, no longer working: inoperative.

entries.clue: Son tucks into a cuppa in the main (2,3)

indicatorNotes.tucks into: the son is tucked inside the other letters

blocks.note: a cuppa is a cup of tea: A TEA
S = son, as in genealogies

annotation.surface: A son helps himself to a cup of tea.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The main' is the old poetic word for the open sea, and 'in the main' usually means 'mostly', which is the disguise.
annotation.definitionFit: A poetic sense: 'the main' is the open ocean, so to be in the main is to be out on the ocean.

entries.clue: Example of popular intellectual attitude (8)

blocks.note: in = popular, fashionable
a stance is a position taken on an issue

annotation.surface: Someone cites a case of the fashionable highbrow pose.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Popular' giving IN is one of the commonest short equivalents in crosswords: what is in is in fashion.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a case in point, the sense kept alive in the phrase 'for example'.

entries.clue: Recall put into motion in Burgundy store? (6)

indicatorNotes.put into motion: the letters are set moving and resettle in a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder

annotation.surface: A product recall is ordered at a shop in Burgundy.
annotation.walkthrough: Burgundy is the French wine, not the colour or the region; the question mark flags that a cellar is only one example of a store for it.
annotation.definitionFit: Wine such as burgundy is stored in a cellar.

entries.clue: Is it possible to get work on yard and awning? (6)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, one piece sits on top of the next

blocks.note: 'can I get...?' asks whether it is possible
op = opus, a work
y = yard, the unit

annotation.surface: Someone asks whether they can get building work done on the yard and a shade fitted.
annotation.walkthrough: The opening question is the whole of CAN, compressed from 'can I get?'. OP for a work comes from opus numbers in music.
annotation.definitionFit: A canopy is a cloth or roof cover, like an awning.

entries.clue: Liberal donor leaving grand fund for city (9)

indicatorNotes.leaving: the G leaves the word, dropped from it

blocks.note: L = Liberal, the political party
a giver is a donor
G = grand, a thousand; removed from GIVER
a pool is a shared fund

annotation.surface: A generous donor withdraws a thousand pounds from a civic fund.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Grand' reads as an adjective praising the donor; it is G, slang for a thousand, taken out of GIVER.
annotation.definitionFit: Liverpool is a city in north-west England.

entries.clue: Trouble in correctional institution judge ignored (3)

indicatorNotes.ignored: the judge's letter is left out

blocks.note: a jail is a prison
J = judge; removed from JAIL

annotation.surface: A prison riot breaks out after a judge's ruling is disregarded.
annotation.walkthrough: Trouble is the verb here, as in 'what ails you?', not a noun about unrest.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym with 'trouble' as a verb: whatever troubles you afflicts you, as an illness does.

entries.clue: Idiot snapping following sacking is sad (13)

indicatorNotes.following sacking: after being sacked, as a city is sacked, the letters lie wrecked and rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters

annotation.surface: A fool loses his temper after being fired, which is a sorry sight.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sacking' in the surface is losing a job; as the instruction it is the plundering of a town. 'Sad' means feeble or poor, as in a sad effort.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Sad' in its informal sense of feeble or pathetic: a sad effort is one that lets you down.

entries.clue: Alumnus sitting in complex (9)

blocks.note: OB = old boy, a former pupil
a sitting is a session

annotation.surface: A former student sits inside some large building complex.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Complex' pictures a building; it is the psychological sense, a fixation.
annotation.definitionFit: A complex is an obsessive preoccupation, as in a guilt complex.

entries.clue: Foul causing injury pushing head right back (4)

indicatorNotes.pushing head right back: the first letter is moved all the way to the end

blocks.note: evil = harmful; its head E then goes to the back

annotation.surface: A footballer commits a foul that injures someone by shoving their head back.
annotation.walkthrough: EVIL with its opening E sent to the end gives the answer. 'Right' means 'all the way', not the direction R.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words mean disgusting or morally repugnant.

entries.clue: State of duck mostly seen in northern area (6)

indicatorNotes.mostly: most of the word, the last letter dropped
indicatorNotes.seen in: the shortened word sits inside the other letters

blocks.note: N = northern
to duck is to evade; EVADE loses its last letter
A = area

annotation.surface: A naturalist reports the condition of a duck spotted up north.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Duck' is the verb, to dodge, not the bird. 'State of' reads as condition; it is a US state.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: one of the fifty US states, home of Las Vegas and much desert.

entries.clue: A person with issue about page in manifest (8)

indicatorNotes.about: PARENT goes about the P, holding it after its first letter

blocks.note: the word itself
issue = offspring, so a person with issue is a parent
p = page

annotation.surface: Someone with a complaint about a page appears on a ship's passenger list.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Issue' reads as a grievance; in the legal sense it means children. 'Manifest' could be a noun, a cargo list, but here it is the adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: Manifest means plainly visible, apparent.

entries.clue: After mixing, use on a gas at absolute zero? (3,1,7)

indicatorNotes.After mixing: mixing blends ingredients until they lose their original order, so the letters come out rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters

annotation.surface: A chemistry instruction: mix, then apply to a gas cooled to absolute zero.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not a sausage' is British slang for nothing at all. The surface keeps to physics, where absolute zero is a temperature, so the idea of 'nothing' stays hidden.
annotation.definitionFit: Not a sausage means nothing whatsoever: absolute zero.

entries.clue: Worker with one explosive thing that levels field? (8)

blocks.note: a hand is a worker, as in farmhand
I = one, the Roman numeral
a cap is a small explosive charge, as in a toy cap gun

annotation.surface: A labourer with a bomb flattening a field.
annotation.walkthrough: The field is the runners in a race, not farmland: a handicap evens their chances. The question mark admits the definition is playful.
annotation.definitionFit: A handicap weights the better competitors to level a field of runners.

entries.clue: Duke one’s seen on track in Converse (9)

indicatorNotes.seen on: in a down clue, the first pieces sit on top of the next

blocks.note: D = duke
one's = I'S, I = one plus the S
a racecourse or running track

annotation.surface: A duke spotted at a racetrack wearing Converse trainers.
annotation.walkthrough: Converse looks like the shoe brand; it is the verb, to talk.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are verbs for talking; the answer adds a sense of talking at length on a subject.

entries.clue: Really dislike stripping, it’s an obscene thing (4)

indicatorNotes.stripping: stripping peels off the outer letters

blocks.note: to loathe is to really dislike; its outer L and E are removed

annotation.surface: Someone who hates striptease declares it obscene.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is about undressing; the stripping is done to LOATHE, losing its first and last letters.
annotation.definitionFit: An oath is a swear word, an obscenity.

entries.clue: Those starting courses left by bread-makers (8)

indicatorNotes.by: beside: the L stands next to the rest

blocks.note: L = left
bread is slang for money, so earners make it

annotation.surface: Novice diners leave the first courses to the bakers.
annotation.walkthrough: Bread-makers look like bakers; bread is slang for money, and those who make it are earners.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: beginners on a course of study; in Britain, L-plates mark novice drivers the same way.

entries.clue: Source of lines one’s found in manuscript (4)

indicatorNotes.found in: one piece is found inside the other

blocks.note: MS = manuscript
one's = I'S, I = one plus the S

annotation.surface: A poet's lines turn up in an old manuscript.
annotation.walkthrough: Lines are a school punishment, a sentence written out many times, and Miss is the teacher who hands them out.
annotation.definitionFit: Miss, the teacher, is the one who sets lines as punishment.

entries.clue: Romantic confession of one leant on that US agency broke (8)

indicatorNotes.broke: the agency broke into the confession, splitting it

blocks.note: 'I list', the speaker admitting to leaning over, as a ship lists
the DEA, the US Drug Enforcement Administration

annotation.surface: A romantic admits confiding in an American agency that went bust.
annotation.walkthrough: The confession is spoken in the first person, which gives I; list is a nautical word for leaning. DEA breaks in between them.
annotation.definitionFit: A romantic is an idealist, one who dreams rather than compromises.

entries.clue: Potential queens getting a fill of royal seafood (6)

indicatorNotes.getting a fill of: the pawns are filled with the R

blocks.note: in chess a pawn can be promoted to a queen
R = royal, as in RN, Royal Navy

annotation.surface: Aspiring queens stuff themselves on a royal seafood feast.
annotation.walkthrough: Potential queens are chess pawns, which can become queens on reaching the far rank.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: these small shellfish are one kind of seafood among many.

entries.clue: Political type of protest singer holding note (8)

indicatorNotes.holding: the singer holds the note inside, where DEMO meets RAT

blocks.note: a demo is a protest march
an informer 'sings' to the police, and is a rat
C, a musical note

annotation.surface: A political sort of protest singer sustains a note.
annotation.walkthrough: The singer is a criminal informer who 'sings' to the police, not a musician; the protest-song surface hides that underworld sense.
annotation.definitionFit: A member of the US party of that name is a political type; with a small d it is anyone who backs rule by the people.

entries.clue: Slightly blue soup (bishop omitted to follow recipe) (6)

indicatorNotes.omitted: the bishop's letter is left out
indicatorNotes.to follow: what remains comes after the R

blocks.note: R = recipe, from the Latin 'recipe', 'take', on prescriptions
bisque is a shellfish soup
B = bishop in chess notation; removed from BISQUE

annotation.surface: A cooking note: a bluish soup, and leave the bishop out of the recipe.
annotation.walkthrough: Blue here means smutty, not the colour. R for recipe comes from old prescriptions.
annotation.definitionFit: Risqué means slightly indecent, a bit blue.

entries.clue: Black market to be stopped by British leader (5)

indicatorNotes.to be stopped by: the B plugs the middle of the word, stopping it up

blocks.note: a sale is a market for goods
B, the leading letter of British

annotation.surface: A British prime minister shuts down the black market.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Black market' reads as one phrase; the definition is 'Black' alone. Sable is the heraldic word for black.
annotation.definitionFit: A heraldic term: on coats of arms black is named after the dark fur of the animal of that name.

entries.clue: Anger reported in The Observer (4)

blocks.note: ire is a literary word for anger; say it out loud

annotation.surface: A newspaper story reports anger in the pages of The Observer.
annotation.walkthrough: The Observer is a British Sunday newspaper, so the surface looks like a press item; here it just means one who observes. In a British accent the two words sound the same.
annotation.definitionFit: An eyer is one who eyes things, an observer.

entries.clue: Foreign capital or country you won’t see me in (3)

indicatorNotes.won’t see: the letters are not seen, so they are removed
indicatorNotes.in: the removed letters were inside the word

blocks.note: Yemen, in Arabia
the word itself; removed from YEMEN

annotation.surface: A traveller names a foreign capital city and a country they refuse to visit.
annotation.walkthrough: Capital suggests a city; it is money. YEMEN loses the ME from its middle.
annotation.definitionFit: The yen is Japan's currency, a foreign capital in the money sense.

entries.clue: Uplifting underwear or drab new pants (9)

indicatorNotes.pants: British slang for rubbish, so the letters are in a bad state

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: A choice between a push-up bra and some dull new knickers.
annotation.walkthrough: Pants are underwear in the surface, which fits perfectly; as the instruction it is British slang for rubbish.
annotation.definitionFit: The Wonderbra is a push-up bra, underwear that uplifts.

entries.clue: Political thinker works well together with nurse (6)

indicatorNotes.together with: the pieces are joined side by side

blocks.note: EN = enrolled nurse
a team that gels works well together

annotation.surface: A political theorist collaborates happily with a nurse.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Works well together' looks like one phrase; 'together with' is the joining word, leaving 'works well' as GELS.
annotation.definitionFit: Friedrich Engels was Marx's co-author, a political thinker.

entries.clue: Music producer strangely terse getting Oscar (6)

indicatorNotes.getting: the O is gained at the end

blocks.note: anagram fodder
Oscar is O in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A curt record producer is handed an Oscar.
annotation.walkthrough: A music producer sounds like a person in a studio; it is the machine that plays music.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by function: a two-speaker sound system is a machine that produces music in the home.
